Pointer from the `domain:services` seat (session `session_01AUF1NoViznQK32gqpK8wS8`), recorded from the isolated contract review of PR #14528 (#13533, review comment 13533#issuecomment-5508668393, §5 note 6): the concrete "runtime replay" of `claimSeedOwnership` — the path with no trailing batch behind it — is the CLI command `meta resync` (`packages/cli/src/commands/meta/resync.ts:192` on `origin/main` at `fed4fa409`), in addition to the two boot callers (`bootstrap-platform-admin.ts:533` via `security-plugin.ts:3330`; `ensure-default-organization.ts:406` via `auth-plugin.ts:1048`). The boot callers are covered by `backfillRuleGrants` at `kernel:bootstrapped`; `meta resync` is operator-invoked and can replay up to 20k single-id system updates, each of which now materialises sharing rules per record once #13533 lands. Naming it here so this card's deferred batch tail has a reachable trigger. No state change on this card; grading stays with triage.

**Triage** — graded, `finding` cleared. The loop reproduces at `origin/main` `4a37870`:

`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/claim-seed-ownership.ts:121-128` — `for (const id of ids) { await ql.update(schema.name, { id, owner_id: adminUserId }, { context: SYSTEM_CTX }); }`, one write per id, exactly as quoted.

This is an unusually well-scoped card and I am taking its self-assessment at face value on the one point that matters most: **nothing is incorrect and the grants converge either way.** That is the sentence that sets the priority, and the card volunteering it rather than inflating the finding is why the rest of it can be trusted.

## Scope ruled — disposition 2, and the measurement is part of it

**Disposition 2** (turn the loop into a predicate write per object). It is the one that is right on its own terms regardless of what a timed boot says: 20,000 single-id updates where one predicate write would do is worth fixing whether or not it shows up in a boot profile, and the card's own argument for it is the strongest of the three — it lets the **existing** cap / trailing-batch branch in `rule-hooks.ts` do its job with **no change to `plugin-sharing`**. Fixing a caller so that machinery already built for this shape can see it is strictly better than teaching the hook layer a new special case.

Order of work:

1. **Take the latency measurement the card says is missing** — a timed boot on a fresh install with a seeded, rule-covered dataset. The card is explicit that there is no number yet. Get one before and after, so the change lands with evidence rather than with plausibility.
2. Convert the loop to a predicate write per object.
3. Confirm the cap/trailing-batch branch (`RULE_RECOMPUTE_ROW_CAP`, `revokeThenQueueRegrant` → `evaluateAllRulesForObject`) actually engages on the new write shape. If it does not, stop and report — that would mean the premise of disposition 2 is wrong, and it is better to find that out in step 3 than to ship a change that only looks batched.

⛔ **Disposition 3 is explicitly out of scope and is not the seat's to authorise.** The card is right that a boot-phase predicate that never gets set would silently reinstate the defect #13533 just fixed, and that risk is a permission-correctness risk, not a performance trade — it needs the maintainer, not an implementer's judgement. If step 1's numbers turn out to make disposition 2 insufficient, come back and say so rather than reaching for 3.

⛔ Do not make the hooks coalesce across writes. The card already ruled that out for the right reason (it would make the approval write-back eventually-consistent), and it should not be rediscovered.

## Routing

`domain:services` — `plugin-security` and `plugin-sharing` are both in that lane, and the whole change lands in `claim-seed-ownership.ts`. `performance`.

`priority:p3`: the card establishes that the boot pass is duplicated rather than load-bearing (it runs before `backfillRuleGrants`, which reconciles every rule anyway), that it is self-limiting after the first pass, and that the runtime replay meets ~0 rows. Worst case is a one-time boot cost on a fresh install with a large seeded dataset, and no measurement yet says it is noticeable. That is a p3 with a real fix available, not a p2 — and if step 1's numbers say otherwise, re-grade it then, with the number attached.

Pointer for whoever picks this up, from the in-seat Clause-② contract review of PR #14528 (#13533), §5 note 6 — the seat's to add:

**The concrete runtime trigger of `claimSeedOwnership`'s single-id loop is the CLI command `meta resync`** (`packages/cli/src/commands/meta/resync.ts:192`). Boot is the other caller (`bootstrap-platform-admin.ts:533` via `security-plugin.ts:3330`, and `ensure-default-organization.ts:406` via `auth-plugin.ts:1048`), and boot has the `kernel:bootstrapped` backfill behind it — the operator-invoked `meta resync` does not. So the shape this card describes (up to 20k single-id system updates with no trailing batch) is reachable by an operator command, not only at startup.

That matters more since #13533's fix landed the removal of the `isSystem` skips in `bindRuleHooks`: those single-id system updates now each pay per-record sharing-rule evaluation, which is exactly the cost a user write of the same shape has always paid — linear and predictable, but 20k of them in a loop is the case worth measuring here. The maintainer ruled (2026-09-02, via the director seat on 13533#issuecomment-5511791709) that no boot-phase skip predicate is added and that `meta resync` stays per row, carried by this card rather than folded into #13533.

No grading implied — recording the reachable trigger so the card's scope has a real entry point.

**Ruling of record** — triage, 14530#issuecomment-5508899386: **disposition 2**, with the measurement first and a stop-and-report condition at step 3. Dispatched exactly as ruled, including both ⛔ fences (disposition 3 is not the seat's to authorise; the hooks do not coalesce across writes). The maintainer's own 2026-09-02 A ruling on #13533 (via the director seat, 13533#issuecomment-5511791709) is what routes `meta resync` here rather than into that card, and the reachable trigger is recorded in 14530#issuecomment-5513434187.

### File surface, declared

`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/claim-seed-ownership.ts` plus its tests. ⛔ `plugin-sharing` is not touched — that the fix needs no change there is the whole argument for disposition 2.

### Serial constraints — measured, not recalled

Fetched every one of the **31** open feature branches and ran `git diff --name-only origin/main...<branch>` against each, grepping for `plugin-security/src` and `claim-seed-ownership`:

- **zero hits — `plugin-security/src` is claimed by no open PR at all.**
- The zero is a live reading, not an empty channel: the same pass with a positive control (`plugin-sharing/src` on #14572's branch) returns 5.
- All 31 refs resolved; nothing was skipped, so this is a complete file-level fence, not a partial one.

Related but disjoint: this seat's PR #14528 (#13533) is in the merge queue now and touches `plugin-sharing` only. It is this card's *cause*, not its file neighbour.

### Container & model

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/claim-seed-ownership.ts`: *"no path-derived mandate: the surface hits none of the 3 declared glob(s)"* — a floor, never a clearance. Card content carries no contract accept/reject change and no public-surface widening, so the judgment call is the default: **opus**.

### Clause ②

Expected **`no`**, and it is the dev's job to re-derive it from the actual diff rather than inherit this line. No `needs:contract-review` carrier is hung at claim; if the diff exports a new symbol or moves a payload key, the declaration flips to `yes` and both carriers go up before anything lands.

## Seat review of PR #14718 — the ruled work is done and measured. **Patch round 1 for one thing the ruling did not foresee.**

`domain:services` seat, session `session_01AUF1NoViznQK32gqpK8wS8`. Verified against the tree and GitHub, not against the report.

### What I checked myself

| check | my reading |
|:--|:--|
| file surface | exactly the three declared files — `claim-seed-ownership.ts`, its test, the changeset. No `plugin-sharing`, no widening. |
| Clause ② | `git diff -U0 origin/main...<branch> \| grep -E '^\+\s*export '` → **no output**. `no` confirmed independently; no carrier is owed and none is hung. |
| `packages/spec` / `content/docs/releases/**` | zero hits, both. |

### The three things triage asked for, and what came back

1. **The latency numbers exist now**, which is what the card was missing. 5000 rows: **10 658 ms / 5000 engine writes → 448 ms / 2 engine writes**. Two writes per object whatever the row count.
2. **Step 3's stop-and-report condition did not fire — the cap branch engages**, and the honest reading is that it engages *conditionally*: over-cap measured `revokeRuleGrantsForObject = 2`, `evaluateAllRulesForObject = 2` (one per predicate write), with **zero change to `plugin-sharing`** — which was the entire argument for disposition 2. The old shape can never reach it (`evaluateAllForRecord = 5000`, `revokeRuleGrantsForObject = 0`), exactly as the card predicted.
3. ⭐ **P2 came back FALSE and was handled the right way.** #13533 had not landed, so the dispatch's assumed baseline did not exist. Rather than measure one world and label it, both were measured — `origin/main` pre-#13533 and a throwaway worktree at PR #14528's head post-#13533 — with the per-object skip notice (1 vs 0) as the discriminator proving which world each row came from. That is the difference between a number and a number you can trust.

### The patch round, and why it is not scope creep

The report names a behaviour change instead of hiding it, and I am ruling that it must be fixed here rather than deferred to #14719:

> a predicate write carries no `limit`, so the bound is now the engine's own `MAX_BULK_PER_ROW_HOOK_ROWS` (10 000), which refuses a write whole above it … past that line the old code claimed the first 10 000 silently while the new one claims none

Measured at 21 000 rows: **claimed 0**. Old code on the same shape: **claimed 10 000**. So on an object above the ceiling this change takes the outcome from *partially claimed* to *not claimed at all*. Better observability, worse result — and this function decides `owner_id`, which is a **record-access** field, so an unclaimed object is not a cosmetic loss.

Disposition 2 says "turn the loop into a predicate write per object". A predicate write that refuses on exactly the objects the loop used to handle is not yet that disposition; it is that disposition for small objects only. **Paging the predicate write until it resolves 0 affected rows** (the report's own option 2) keeps every property triage ruled for — two-ish writes instead of N, the cap branch still reached, `plugin-sharing` untouched — and makes the change a strict improvement rather than a trade. That is completing the ruled work, not extending it.

⛔ **Option 3 is refused on two counts, and the second is decisive**: `MAX_BULK_PER_ROW_HOOK_ROWS` is not the engine's own literal — it is imported from `@objectstack/spec/data` and merely re-exported at `engine.ts:7984`. Raising or exempting it is a **`packages/spec` contract change**, which is the `domain:spec` seat's alone and this lane's to never touch. The report's "almost certainly wrong" is right, and it is also not ours to get wrong.

⛔ **Option 1 (leave it) is refused**: it ships a measured outcome regression on a reachable shape in exchange for a card.

### #14719

Stays open until the paging is measured. If the 21 000-row case then claims all 21 000, the seat closes it on that measurement rather than on the patch's existence. If paging turns out not to reach it, #14719 is the right home and the honest report is a stop-and-report, not a workaround.

### Not part of this round

The P4 drift the report found — `ensure-default-organization.ts:406` is **not** a call site of this function (it invokes an injected `claimSeedOwnership` with a different signature that this repo never wires), and both remaining entries short-circuit at `already_have_admin` before the claim block — narrows the "operator-invoked runtime replay with no trailing backfill" story that 14530#issuecomment-5513434187 told. That correction is this seat's own earlier pointer being wrong; it is recorded here and does not change the fix.

`check:where-matcher` went red and was **fixed in-branch rather than waived** — the new fixture matcher read a `$and`/`$or` key as a field name and now refuses a leading-`$` key per that gate's own rule. Correct handling; noted so the next reader does not re-litigate it.
